items.title: Weather alert again issued for Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: For the second night in a row, Mississauga and Brampton are under a weather alert. Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory for the cities. Additionally, it covers St. Catharines, Grimsby, Niagara Falls, Welland, and Niagara Region as a whole. “Patchy frost is expected tonight, particularly for inland areas,” Environment Canada said. “Take preventative measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees, and crops. ” It’s the latest of several frost advisories issued by Environment Canada this week. Areas shaded in yellow are under a frost advisory from Environment Canada. Patchy frost is expected overnight, mainly for areas away from the lakes. Forecasters are predicting a low of 2 C. (Credit: Environment Canada) As mentioned, last night Mississauga and Brampton were impacted.

items.title: Machine gun, cocaine and other drugs found during police search of Mississauga home
items.summary: A Mississauga man faces numerous charges after police found a machine gun, other firearms and a huge stash of hard drugs during the search of a home in the city’s north end earlier this month. Peel Regional Police said officers executed a search warrant on Oct. 10 at a residence near Winston Churchill Boulevard and Derry Road in the Meadowvale area of Mississauga. Officers involved in the search discovered a 9mm automatic machine gun, three handguns and a large quantity of drugs including cocaine, crack cocaine, methamphetamine, cannabis, hashish and prescription pills, police said. The seized drugs are valued at $70,000, police added. So far this year, 136 firearms have been seized by Peel police officers. Detectives with the Peel police 11 Division Community Intervention Response Team launched an investigation in September following community complaints about drug trafficking in the northwest part of the city. The probe culminated in the Oct. 10 search and subsequent arrest of a suspect. Officers with the 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau were also invovled in the police operation.

items.title: House of the week: Large home with theatre and upgraded kitchen in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: Large home with a custom theatre and upgraded kitchen. Features: This home offers over 6,000 square feet of total living space with a stately facade and three-car garage. Inside, features include soaring and coffered ceilings, expansive windows, pot lights and wainscotting. At the centre, the kitchen boasts built-in stainless steel appliances, granite counters, custom cabinetry, a custom backsplash, a pantry and a large centre island. The breakfast area has a walk-out to the deck and a two-way gas fireplace shared with the family room. The formal living room showcases a dramatic circular tray ceiling, while the dining room features an elegant recessed tray ceiling with statement lighting. Upstairs, the primary bedroom has vaulted ceilings, his and hers closets, and a five-piece ensuite bathroom with dual sinks, a soaker tub and a walk-in shower. Four additional bedrooms with dedicated closet space and ensuite bathrooms complete this level. Two staircases add convenience and flexibility. The finished walk-up basement has a recreation room, a custom theatre and gym. Outside, the professionally landscaped and fully fenced backyard offers privacy with a deck and patio.

items.title: Construction begins on major upgrade to large park in Mississauga
items.summary: Construction has begun to significantly upgrade a large park in Mississauga’s east end, the city said this week. Mississauga Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca said in an update to the community that “construction is underway” at popular Garnetwood Park, where a number of amenities are being added. The “concrete forming” phase of the project, where crews build the formwork (molds into which concrete will later be poured), began earlier this month. Workers are now onto the next stage, where construction moves forward. Fonseca said earlier the City of Mississauga is adding “incredible amenities” to the 34-acre park located alongside Etobicoke Creek, near Burnhamthorpe Road East and Ponytrail Drive. The green space already features basketball nets, a leash-free zone, mobile food vendor, multi-use court, a playground, soccer field, softball diamond and a renovated spray pad, in addition to a new four-court tennis facility that opened last year. Acting on feedback from the community, the city is now adding two new paved paths to the trail system, new four-season seating/tables, a seasonal ice rink surface and pickleball courts. The upgraded spray pad was completed this past summer. Neither Fonseca nor City of Mississauga officials have provided a specific timeline for completion of the other amenities. The City of Mississauga, along with Tennis Canada and National Bank, opened the renovated Garnetwood Park Tennis Courts in June 2025. The four-court tennis facility received the makeover through National Bank’s Play Your Court program.

MiWay, the City of Mississauga’s public transit provider, said in an online update the following routes will be on detour until early Monday morning: Map shows area where work is ongoing on the Hazel McCallion Line in Mississauga. The marked area, Hurontario Street from Burnhamthorpe Road to Eglinton Avenue, will see increased construction activity through the end of December. Temporary road closures are expected over the course of the next couple of months, and potentially beyond.

items.title: Brr-ing on the cold: Get your home winter-ready with these fall maintenance tips
items.summary: As winter rolls in, it can bring some risks to your property. Taking time to inspect your home and yard can help protect against weather-related damage. As Mississauga trades summer sunshine for sweater weather, falling leaves and crisp autumn days, now is the time to prepare for what comes next: winter. Before colder temperatures set in, take time to inspect and clean your property to help protect against weather-related challenges. Being proactive before temperatures drop can help prevent costly damage from colder conditions. This critical upkeep acts as a preventive measure to protect against fire damage (from heating sources), water damage (from frozen pipes) and structural damage (from wind, ice and snow buildup), while helping ensure your home and property are well maintained. Start by winterizing your home and yard. Here are a few ways to protect your property and keep it safe, warm and comfortable through the winter months. Help protect your home from winter weather by ensuring eavestroughs and downspouts are free of leaves, pine needles, sticks and other debris. Keeping them clear ensures proper drainage and helps prevent leaks and water damage. Consider disconnecting roof downspouts from pipes connected to your basement weepers, which help drain water away from your foundation. Instead, direct the runoff onto your lawn or garden using an elbow and downspout extension, ensuring water drains at least three feet away from your home’s foundation. Pruning trees and hedges before winter promotes healthy spring growth, helps prevent damage from heavy snowfall and improves the appearance of your landscape. Storing rain barrels and turning off outdoor faucets helps conserve water, prevent flooding and protect plumbing from freezing.

items.title: Want to manage an ice rink this winter in Mississauga? City opens volunteer applications for residents
items.summary: Although weather-dependent, the natural ice rink season is expected to begin mid-December and last through March 2027. The City of Mississauga is looking for volunteers to maintain natural ice rinks in city parks between December to January, depending on the weather. If you’re interested in ice skating close to home this year, the City of Mississauga is accepting volunteer applications for its natural ice rink program. The program is community volunteer-run and provides residents with free outdoor places to skate and play hockey. According to the city, 102 volunteers participated in last year’s winter program to maintain local ice rinks across the city. Applications are being accepted until Nov. 15. To manage a rink, a minimum of three volunteers are required for daily upkeep. Volunteers are expected to maintain the ice, clear snow after winter weather events, monitor ice conditions and handle general rink maintenance. The city provides all necessary equipment, including access to a heated rink hut with a water hydrant, hoses, spray nozzles, ice scrapers, signage and maintenance instructions.
